Switches: SKILL_DRAFT_PUBLISH and SKILL_BUNDLE_RETENTION, both on capability-core, both read strictly (only the literal "true" turns them on), both default off. With both off, every statement, route and body is as before. One exception: the bundle reads now also filter on `state`. That changes nothing while every row is live, which is always the case with retention off.

What was built:
- **Session-core migration 0110** adds `draft` (JSONB, NULL or an object), `draft_updated_at` and `draft_by` to `agent_skills`. It replaces 0109's revision snapshot with the same keys plus a `has_draft` boolean (never the draft text). Ships a revert file.
- **Capability-core migration 0037** adds `skill_bundles.state` (live, draft, superseded). The old unique index on (org, skill) is swapped for a partial one on live rows under the SAME name. This matters because 0021 re-runs at every boot with CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS: if the old full index came back while superseded rows exist, boot would fail. Also adds a one-draft-per-skill index and a unique (org, skill, manifest) index. Carries a contract marker and a down file.
- **Drafts in `registry_apis.go`** (switch on):
  - A PATCH of an accepted skill's text writes the draft. The draft starts from the live fields (session-core's version body function).
  - New routes: POST `.../publish`, DELETE `.../draft`, POST `.../versions/{v}/restore`. All are owner-or-admin and answer with the typed error envelope.
  - Publish lints the draft, then makes it live in one statement that clears it, so the trigger cuts the version. A name clash returns 409.
  - Restore writes the old version's body into the draft only. The old bundle comes back only with retention on and only while the skill still holds it.
  - Reads carry `draft`, `draft_updated_at` and `draft_by`; the list response carries `drafts_enabled: true`.
  - With retention on, a skill delete removes all of its bundles (D2-382).
- **Retention in `store.go`**:
  - Put and Delete mark the old live bundle superseded instead of deleting it. Re-uploading bytes the skill already holds reuses that row.
  - With drafts also on, an upload to an accepted skill becomes the draft's bundle.
  - Garbage collection keeps superseded bundles named by a version or by the skill's draft.
  - New helpers: `ManifestAt`, `PublishDraftBundle`, `DiscardDraftBundle`, `DeleteSkillBundles`, `HeldManifest`.
- **Pinned bundle reads**:
  - `server.go` honours the new `manifest_sha256` request field only while retention is on, and refuses a value that is not a hex digest.
  - `capabilities.proto`: `GetSkillBundleManifestRequest` gains `manifest_sha256 = 2` (additive, commented).
  - execution-core asks for the exact bundle the gateway named.
  - In the gateway, `skill_file` reads the pinned version's bundle when the skill changed since the run pinned it (only while MODEL_GATEWAY_SKILL_PINS is on). If that bundle is no longer kept, the tool says so rather than returning the live files.
- **BFF**: three pass-through routes with `update_skill`'s authority.
- **Frontend**: four new action contracts (`skills.draft.save`, `skills.publish`, `skills.draft.discard`, `skills.version.restore`); a Draft badge with Publish and Discard draft; "Restore as draft" in the history drawer, shown only when the listing says drafts are on.

depth_findings.text: SKILL_BUNDLE_RETENTION keeps superseded bundles readable through GetSkillBlob/ManifestAt, which any org member can reach today (D2-379/D2-383), so it must stay off until those are fixed.

Retention garbage collection keeps a superseded bundle only when some agent_skill_versions.bundle_sha256 names it, and that column is stamped only while SKILL_VERSIONS_API is on, so turning on SKILL_BUNDLE_RETENTION without SKILL_VERSIONS_API retains nothing.
Draft bundles need both SKILL_BUNDLE_RETENTION and SKILL_DRAFT_PUBLISH; with drafts on and retention off, a bundle upload still goes live at once and publish ignores the draft's bundle_sha256.

PATCH under drafts lints the live row with the patch laid over it, not the existing draft; publish re-lints the draft, so enforce still holds, but a report-mode finding on PATCH can describe the wrong base text.

skill_file compares the run's pin digest with the gateway skill cache (TTL up to 60 s), so for up to one TTL after a publish a pinned run can read the new live bundle before the cache shows the change.

The gateway's /skills mounts (skill_mounts_for_turn) still name the live bundle from ListSkillBundles at turn start, not the pinned version's bundle_sha256; this is correct within one turn, but a resumed Do run would mount the current bundle.

Not run: edit a live skill under SKILL_DRAFT_PUBLISH (turns keep v2), publish (v3 pinned next turn), restore v1 as draft and publish (v4 with v1's body digest), re-upload a bundle with retention on and read the old file through skill_file from a run pinned before; plus apply-and-revert of session-core 0110 and capability-core 0037 on PG16 and a boot re-run of 0021 after 0037 with superseded rows present.

There are no capability-core integration tests (testcontainers) for putRetained, PublishDraftBundle or the GC against a real agent_skill_versions table (TestGCKeepsBlobsOfPinnedVersions in the design); the unit tests check statements only.

The design's 'drop skill_bundles_org_skill_uq' became a same-name swap to the partial index, because capability-core re-runs 0021 at every boot and would otherwise rebuild the full unique index and fail on retained rows.

SKILL_EXT_POLICY_ENFORCED reads the org policy cache that admit_turn fills only when ORG_AGENT_POLICY_MODE=enforce; with the policy mode off or shadow, turning it on withholds every authored skill (fail closed by design), so the two switches must be turned on together.

The Space write half needs a Control decision kind 'Space skill write' plus a capability-core verifier; until then every Space POST/PATCH/DELETE answers 403 space_skill_decision_required and no Space row can exist outside a hand-written DB row.

reattach_skill and skill_file (usable_skill_named) resolve only the org catalogue, so a matched Space skill cannot be recovered or have its bundle read mid-run; chat_turn_registry ratings never credit Space skills.
Operator-pushed (gRPC UpsertSkill) and disk-loaded skills count as first-party and are never narrowed by ext.skills, because ext_skills_permits keys on the session-core source prefix.
SkillStore.thread_spaces grows one entry per (org, caller, thread) with no eviction, like the existing `loaded` map; it needs a sweep before Space threads are heavy.

The slice is built behind SESSION_CORE_API_KEY_PRINCIPAL. The switch is off by default and read with mp_contracts::loop_fold::switch_from. Nothing was compiled or run (code-first). The patch is at C:/dev/CoresSystem/.claude/worktrees/epic-shaw-4d613b/.plan-work/execution/patches/W3-22/EP-12-S4.patch (46,513 bytes). All three files are LF, not CRLF as the notes said, and they stay LF.

What changed in auth.rs:
- New PrincipalKind::ApiKey. validate_identity(claims, accept_api_key) gets an "api_key" arm that uses the gateway's and inference-core's exact shape rules. It also refuses three things: a persistent key token of a ZDR org, a waiver on a key token, and a key_id on any other token type while the switch is on. key_id and acting_user_id are decoded as raw serde Values, so with the switch off every token decodes exactly as before.
- The identity of a key has user_id None, principal_id apikey:<key_id> and acting_user_id kept for attribution only. New accessors: is_api_key, api_key_id, acting_user_id, and owner_id (the person for a user, the key principal for a key, None for a service).
- authorize_user now compares against owner_id, which is byte-identical for users and services. authorize_owner_row refuses a key on any row it does not own, including the org-wide read of system-owned rows.
- Enforcement happens in JwtVerifier::intercept. tonic does not give interceptors the call's URI, so a new RpcPathStamp<S> wrapper puts the gRPC path into the request extensions. Only SessionCore and RunService are wrapped. On any unwrapped service the path is absent and a key is refused.
- The closed list API_KEY_METHODS: SessionCore CreateThread, AppendMessage, StartRun and ListConversation; RunService GetRun, ListRuns and CancelRun.
- Every other method answers permission_denied, and so does a key token without the agent:runs scope. A ZDR key gets zdr_feature_not_supported with feature agent_api (FailedPrecondition) on the four write methods.
- No terminal RPC is listed: model-gateway terminalizes runs with its own service token (session_flow.rs service_request), not the caller's bearer.
- A key can neither give nor be a Data Plane delegation.

What changed in grpc.rs:
- create_thread and start_run use caller.owner_id(), so a key owns its own threads and runs.
- start_run calls the new start_run_inner_stamped(..., ApiKeyStamp::of(&caller)). start_run_inner keeps its signature and passes None, so retention_receipt.rs is not touched.
- Appending to a key-owned thread extracts no memory candidates.
- The serve() builder wraps the SessionCore and RunService servers in RpcPathStamp.

What changed in run_origin_stamp.rs: origin_at_birth(user_id, inherited, api_key). A key's run is stamped origin "api" plus api_key_id and api_key_owner. An inherited token still wins as the origin, and a key's run keeps the attribution fields either way.
